I disclose that impairment. That artifact is also the only carrier of the threshold fact — POL-RD-01 forbids citing trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, and the fare meter is derived from the same trace — so under POL-GEN-02(2) the Judge's confidence cannot exceed 0.30, below the 0.70 platform floor, and POL-RD-10(1) requires escalation rather than a final ruling, with the disputed sum held rather than refunded. I accept that the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (no gap over 90 seconds, a jump under 500 m, a 10-second sampling interval); this is a confidence cap, not a data failure, and the two things must be said separately.

No traffic advisory was issued for the CTE on the evening of 18 July 2026: EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact, and the driver's contemporaneous explanation in the chat ('cte very jam tonight boss') is a general assertion that traffic was bad and cannot discharge his burden under POL-RD-08. He does not ask the tribunal to invent an advisory and does not press POL-RD-03. But a closure defence asserted where the only artifact that could carry it is missing from the pool is exactly the trigger in POL-RD-10(5), and the missing artifact carries nothing adverse to him either: on this record the traffic is unknown, not exculpatory, and the answer is a human reviewer, not a refund.

The rider's 60-day record is five deviation claims with one substantiated, which engages POL-RD-08's corroboration requirement because the excess here is 25.5%, below the 30% line: the claim then needs corroboration beyond the gps_trace from the POL-RD-07(ii) list. Every distance figure the rider can point to is a copy or a meter reading of the platform's single distance measurement — 17.6 km on the trip record is the rounded convenience copy POL-RD-01 forbids citing, and 17.6 km on the fare breakdown is the same measurement on the meter. The driver's own statement admits the route, but the route has never been in dispute; it supplies no independent measurement of the excess, which is what the rider must corroborate.

The rider's complaint folds the 1.35 surge multiplier — SGD 9.28 of the SGD 36.60 charged — into the loss. The multiplier is a booking-time line recorded only on the fare breakdown and is not a consequence of the route driven; POL-RD-02 applies it to the recomputed optimal-route fare, so it cannot be presented as deviation damage.

The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp_gantries empty), no tolls (tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. There is accordingly no pass-through correction and no phantom gantry or wrongly applied surcharge for POL-RD-09 to add on top of any distance figure, and the rider's exposure is confined to the distance-and-time line alone.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: here is what the evidence shows and how the fare was recalculated.

1) Was the route off? Yes. The platform's routing engine set the optimal route at 14.0 km (CTE southbound), and the GPS trace measures the route actually driven at 17.57 km. That is an excess of 3.57 km, or 25.5%. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (over 0.8 km and over 20% of optimal), so a deviation is established. It does not reach materiality (not over 50%, not over 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: I accept the driver-side point that his record is 1 deviation flag in 619 completed 90-day trips - below both the 3-flag count and the 0.05 ratio - so there is no repeat-pattern FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. His lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter is context only under POL-GEN-01 and is not used.

2) The GPS trace, both things. The pre-pass tagged EV-GPS-00107 IMPAIRED at weight 0.30 with issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath outlier at 21:44:57 on the Raffles Place approach, implying impossible speeds). For policy purposes it is NOT impaired: POL-RD-07 needs a gap over 90 s, a jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval over 30 s, and it has none (no gaps, 10 s sampling, 331.8 m worst jump). The deviation may therefore be established on it. The finding also survives the 0.30 discount, because the driver's own admission of the route - his contemporaneous chat reply in the trip window and his statement that he went 'by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it' - independently carries the deviation, so under POL-GEN-02(2) the confidence cap is the maximum of the independent carriers, not the trace's 0.30. POL-RD-10(1) is not triggered. I reject the driver-side escalation claim (cap fixed at 0.30) and the driver-side point that the admission corroborates nothing (POL-RD-07(ii) and POL-RD-08 name a driver admission in the chat log and a counterparty statement admitting the route as independent corroboration, which is what the rider-profile serial-claimant test additionally requires here).

3) No exoneration. No traffic advisory was issued (EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing and no closure-adjusted optimal can be built. A general assertion that the CTE was jammed does not discharge the driver's burden under POL-RD-08, and no exculpatory clause was invoked against a cited missing artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not triggered either. There was no rider-requested detour (no rider instruction, waypoint_hint null), so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply.

4) The arithmetic (POL-RD-02). charged_total = SGD 36.60. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 = (21.02 x 1.35) + 0.80 = SGD 29.177. Refund = 36.60 - 29.177 = SGD 7.423, rounded UP to SGD 7.45. The 1.35 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier - a booking-time line, not deviation damage, and it is applied inside the recomputation rather than refunded on its own. There are no ERP gantries, tolls, airport surcharges, waiting fees or promo discounts, so POL-RD-09 adds no pass-through correction and the rider's exposure is the distance-and-time line alone.

Outcome: the rider is refunded SGD 7.45 (PARTIAL_REFUND); the rest of the metered charge stands. No driver compensation is due - the billed 17.6 km matches the trace, so there is no unbilled shortfall. No referrals.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
